title: Hyderabad retired woman allegedly loses ₹33.4 lakh to 'digital arrest' fraud, cyber police probe
date_note: The420.in says the woman complained to Hyderabad cybercrime police on 23 November; the fraud itself began in August.
geo_basis: city stated by source (victim's locality Masab Tank, Hyderabad)
summary: The420.in reports that a retired woman in Hyderabad allegedly lost ₹33.4 lakh after callers posing as police officers told her she faced arrest over a bank account used for money laundering. She complained to Hyderabad cybercrime police, who registered a case under the IT Act and other provisions. The article says no recovery has been announced.
plain: A retired woman in Hyderabad allegedly lost ₹33.4 lakh to callers posing as police officers who threatened her with arrest. Police have registered a case; no recovery has been announced.
exec: Impersonation 'digital arrest' calls are reported to be draining individuals' savings; Hyderabad police have registered a case.
action: As the article notes, police cannot place anyone under digital arrest or demand money for verification over telephone calls.
impact: No recovery of the money has been announced, per The420.in.

evidence.quote: allegedly lost ₹33.4 lakh after cybercriminals impersonating police officers

validation.note: Only The420.in was read; no police statement page was found.
